original_question: Is it true that if a normal subgroup A of a Sylow p-subgroup of a p-soluble finite group G has exponent pe, then the normal closure of A in G has(p, e)-bounded(or even e-bounded) p-length?
target_in_paper: Problem 21.64 in the section "New Problems (21st issue, 2026)" of The Kourovka Notebook. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))
correct_elements: The draft already captures the exact core content of Problem 21.64: a finite p-soluble group G, a normal subgroup A of a Sylow p-subgroup, the hypothesis that A has exponent p^e, and the question whether the normal closure of A in G has (p,e)-bounded p-length, with the stronger possibility of an e-bounded bound. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))
missing_details: Make the universal quantification explicit: for every prime p, every integer e >= 0, every finite p-soluble group G, every Sylow p-subgroup P of G, and every normal subgroup A of P of exponent p^e.
Introduce notation for the Sylow subgroup, e.g. P in Syl_p(G), rather than leaving "a Sylow p-subgroup" unnamed.
Define the normal closure explicitly as A^G = <A^g | g in G>.
Define the p-length l_p(X): the minimal number of p-group factors in a normal series of the finite p-soluble group X whose remaining factors are p'-groups.
Spell out that "(p,e)-bounded" means bounded above by some function f(p,e) independent of the particular choices of G, P, and A.
Spell out that "e-bounded" asks whether the bound can be chosen independent of p.
Correct the exponent notation to p^e.
No ambient field/ring, homogeneity, degree restriction, or asymptotic qualifier occurs in the source; those categories are inapplicable here and should not be added.
refined_question: For every prime p and integer e >= 0, let G be a finite p-soluble group, let P be a Sylow p-subgroup of G, and let A be a normal subgroup of P of exponent p^e. If A^G = <A^g | g in G> denotes the normal closure of A in G, is the p-length l_p(A^G) bounded above by a function of p and e alone? More strongly, can one choose such a bound to depend only on e and not on p? Here l_p(X) denotes the minimal number of p-group factors in a normal series of the finite p-soluble group X whose other factors are p'-groups.
justification: arXiv:1401.0300 is the continuously updated Kourovka Notebook, and the draft matches Problem 21.64 essentially verbatim. The only sharpening needed is to make the universal quantifiers, the notation A^G for normal closure, the definition of p-length, and the meaning of "(p,e)-bounded" / "e-bounded" explicit. This also keeps the question narrower than the older, broader Wilson problem 9.68 about bounding p-length for all finite p-soluble groups whose Sylow p-subgroups lie in a proper variety. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))
